newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker as U.S. market softens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker as U.S. market softens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, pulled lower by a decline in U.S. Treasury prices, with Tuesday's federal budget having little impact on the Canadian market, analysts said.

"It's more a factor of the U.S. than anything. We've done better than the U.S. today but I wouldn't say there's anything huge going on," said a trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "There's fairly light volumes."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.25 to C$113.80 to yield 6.858 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 14/32 to yield 6.58 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 28 basis points from 30 basis points on Tuesday.

Canadian bonds firmed slightly following the release of the budget on Tuesday but the news had little effect in overseas trading. Analysts said the narrowing of long bond spreads today was due more to the fact that the U.S. Treasuries were experiencing brisk selling.
"I think it (the buget) was exactly what was expected with no surprises," said the trader. "We're tracking the U.S. and the U.S. is maybe a little bit heavy."

Canadian bond investors are now looking ahead to the release of details of the Government of Canada's five-year auction on February 26. Details of the auction will be released at 1530 EST/2030 GMT on Thursday.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.35 to C$105.70 to yield 6.211 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.31 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 10 basis points from 11 basis points on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.90 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.09 percent.
